about.title: Santa Rosa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Rosa sits where US-101 threads through the heart of Sonoma County, and much of the city's daily traffic funnels onto that freeway along with Santa Rosa Avenue, Stony Point Road and Route 12. In 2025, the city recorded 562 injury collisions, with 790 people hurt and 8 lives lost. Public records show reported crashes cluster on Tuesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., when the evening commute is at its heaviest. If you were one of the people injured, the days afterward can feel chaotic: medical appointments, a damaged car, and calls from an insurance adjuster you did not expect. LawProactive exists to take one task off your plate. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent California attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery. Reach out when you are ready, and we will help you get a conversation started.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Rosa Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is shorter than you might think
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city bus, county truck or other government vehicle was involved, a claim may need to be filed within six months. Getting connected early keeps those options open.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you shared some blame for the crash. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of responsibility, which is one reason a recorded statement to the other insurer should wait until you have counsel.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case. LawProactive charges you nothing for the connection itself.

items.question: The other driver's insurer called and wants a recorded statement about my US-101 crash. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and doing so before you understand your injuries can work against you. Adjusters may use your words to argue you were partly at fault, which matters under California's comparative fault system. It is reasonable to politely decline until you have spoken with an attorney.

items.question: What evidence should I hold on to after a car accident in Santa Rosa?
items.answer: Keep the police report number, photos of the vehicles and the scene, contact information for witnesses, and every medical record and bill. Do not repair or dispose of your vehicle before it has been documented, and save any texts or emails from insurers. An attorney can help gather items you may not be able to obtain on your own, such as traffic camera footage or the other driver's phone records.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim if my crash happened in Sonoma County?
items.answer: For most car accidents in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity, such as the City of Santa Rosa, Sonoma County or a state agency, may be responsible, a formal claim often must be presented within six months. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to connect with an attorney well before either one approaches.
